makaleler.baslik: Procalcitonin-Informed Decision-Making in Abdominal and Emergency Surgery: A WSES Position Paper.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Abdominal ve Acil Cerrahide Proalsitonin Destekli Karar Verme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: WSES pozisyon raporunda, abdominal ve acil cerrahide prokalsitonin kılavuzluğundaki karar verme süreçleri 6 klinik senaryo üzerinden incelenmiştir. Seri prokalsitonin takibinin, klinik değerlendirme ile entegre edildiğinde antibiyotik kesilmesini destekleyebileceği belirtilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet: Background: Procalcitonin (PCT) may support decision-making in abdominal and emergency surgery when infection is difficult to distinguish from non-infectious inflammation. Its interpretation remains challenging because clinical settings, sampling schedules, and proposed thresholds vary. This WSES position paper examines the evidence across six clinical scenarios to provide a practical framework for PCT-informed decision-making. Methods: A structured literature review covering January 1980 to December 2025, with targeted updates through August 2026, informed six PICO-based clinical questions. Evidence appraisal drew on selected GRADE domains, including consistency, directness, and precision. Recommendations were developed through iterative expert review and consensus. Results: The panel formulated six conditional recommendations addressing intra-abdominal infection diagnosis, antibiotic discontinuation after source control, suspected source-control failure, infected pancreatic necrosis, infectious complications after trauma, and postoperative anastomotic leak. The panel's qualitative assessment rated evidence certainty as moderate for antibiotic discontinuation and the pancreatitis domain, and low for the remaining domains. Serial PCT trends may complement clinical assessment in selected patients. Evidence for reduced antibiotic exposure with predefined PCT algorithms is more established than evidence that PCT-informed imaging, reintervention, or discharge decisions improve patient outcomes. Conclusions: PCT-informed decision-making in abdominal surgery may contribute to a more individualized approach to emergency surgical care and precision emergency surgery. When interpreted as part of serial assessment and integrated with clinical judgement, organ-dysfunction trends, microbiology, imaging, and evaluation of source-control adequacy, PCT may support individualized antibiotic discontinuation, potentially earlier recognition of an unfavourable clinical course, and more timely diagnostic and source-control reassessment. Current evidence does not support universal thresholds or routine serial testing in all surgical patients. Biomarker kinetics should strengthen, but not replace, surgical reasoning or independently determine antimicrobial, imaging, or interventional decisions. Future research should validate setting-specific thresholds and sampling schedules, establish whether PCT provides actionable information before clinical deterioration, and evaluate the clinical effects and cost-effectiveness of PCT-informed pathways.

makaleler.baslik: Timing of Emergency General Surgery After Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Akut Pulmoner Emboli Sonrası Acil Genel Cerrahi Zamanlaması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 1309175 akut pulmoner emboli hastasından acil genel cerrahi uygulanan 3785 hastanın incelendiği çalışmada, majör advers olaylar için 60 günlük bir dönüm noktası saptanmıştır. Akut pulmoner emboliden en az 60 gün sonra yapılan cerrahinin daha düşük advers olay oranı ile ilişkili olduğu gösterilmiştir (OR 0,45; %95 CI 0,37-0,55).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of emergency general surgery (EGS) after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is uncertain, and elective noncardiac surgery guidelines provide limited guidance for this high-acuity population.
STUDY DESIGN: Adults hospitalized with a principal diagnosis of acute PE who subsequently underwent EGS were identified in the 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Time from PE discharge to EGS was modeled using restricted cubic splines. Major adverse events (MAE), complications, readmission, and resource use were evaluated across operative risk and open/laparoscopic approach subgroups.
RESULTS: Among 1,309,175 acute PE hospitalizations, 3,785 (0.3%) underwent subsequent EGS within the calendar year of index hospitalization. Risk-adjusted analysis identified a 60-day inflection point for MAE; 52.4% underwent EGS within 60 days and were classified as Early, with remaining patients classified as Delayed. Compared with Early, Delayed EGS was associated with lower odds of MAE (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.45; 95% CI 0.37-0.55) and lower rates of thromboembolic, cardiac, and respiratory complications, readmission, and resource use. This association persisted across operative risk categories and surgical approaches.
CONCLUSIONS: EGS performed at least 60 days after acute PE was associated with fewer adverse events and lower resource use. When clinically feasible, timing after PE may be an important consideration in planning EGS.
makaleler.dergi_tam: Journal of the American College of Surgeons

turk.baslik: A multidimensional approach to frailty in emergency surgery for perforated peptic ulcer.
turk.baslik_tr: Perfore Peptik Ülser Acil Cerrahisinde Kırılganlığa Çok Boyutlu Yaklaşım
turk.kisa_ozet: Perforasyon nedeniyle acil cerrahi uygulanan 97 hastanın dahil olduğu retrospektif kohort çalışmasında, hastaların %30,9'unun sarkopenik olduğu saptanmıştır. Çok değişkenli analizde, ileri yaş (OR 1,07, p=0,010) ve düşük serum albümin düzeyi (OR 0,75, p<0,001) mortalitenin en güçlü bağımsız öngörücüleri olarak belirlenmiştir.
turk.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Perforated peptic ulcer (PPU) remains a high-risk surgical emergency. Although sarcopenia has been proposed as an objective surrogate of frailty, its independent prognostic value in emergency surgery is unclear. This study evaluated sarcopenia within a multidimensional frailty framework incorporating nutritional, inflammatory, and clinical parameters.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent emergency surgery for PPU at a tertiary center. Sarcopenia was assessed using computed tomography-derived psoas muscle area and psoas muscle index with population-specific cut-off values. Immunonutritional and inflammatory indices (hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet [HALP], neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR], platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], and systemic immune-inflammation index [SII]) were calculated from admission laboratory data. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and discriminatory performance.
RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients were included; 30.9% were sarcopenic. Sarcopenic patients exhibited lower serum albumin, higher inflammatory markers, higher clinical severity scores, and longer intensive care unit and hospital stays (all p<0.05). However, sarcopenia was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality. In multivariable analysis, advanced age (odds ratio [OR] 1.07, p=0.010) and low serum albumin (OR 0.75, p<0.001) were the strongest independent predictors of mortality. Low HALP score and elevated NLR and PLR were significantly associated with sarcopenia. ROC analysis showed that age and albumin had superior discriminatory ability for mortality compared with morphometric muscle parameters.
CONCLUSION: In PPU surgery, frailty is better characterized as a multidimensional biological phenotype rather than isolated muscle loss. While sarcopenia reflects increased vulnerability, mortality risk is more strongly driven by age and nutritional-inflammatory reserve. Integrated frailty assessment may improve risk stratification in emergency surgical patients.

tez.baslik: Mezenterik iskemi yönetiminde eritropoetin kullanımının etkisi
tez.baslik_tr: Mezenterik İskemi Yönetiminde Eritropoetin Kullanımının Etkisi
tez.kisa_ozet: Yirmi dört erişkin erkek Sprague-Dawley sıçanı üzerinde yapılan deneysel çalışmada, süperior mezenterik arter 30 dakika oklüde edilip 60 dakika reperfüze edilmiştir. Reperfüzyon başında uygulanan 3000 IU/kg eritropoetin, iskemi-reperfüzyon hasarında nekroz parametresini anlamlı düzeyde azaltmıştır (p_Bonf=0,026).
tez.ozet: Amaç: Akut mezenterik iskemi, mortalitesi yüksek bir cerrahi acildir; kan akımı yeniden sağlandığında ortaya çıkan iskemi-reperfüzyon hasarı doku yıkımını artırabilir. Bu çalışmada, sıçanlarda oluşturulan deneysel intestinal iskemi-reperfüzyon modelinde eritropoietinin koruyucu etkisinin histopatolojik olarak değerlendirilmesi amaçlanmıştır. Gereç ve Yöntem: 24 adet erişkin erkek Sprague-Dawley sıçanı, her grupta 8 hayvan olacak şekilde sham, iskemi-reperfüzyon (İ/R) ve İ/R + eritropoietin gruplarına ayrıldı. Örneklem büyüklüğü G*Power 3.1.9.7 ile a priori güç analiziyle belirlendi (Cohen f=0,72; α=0,05; 1−β=0,80; N=24; gerçek güç 0,84). Süperior mezenterik arter 30 dakika oklüde edilip 60 dakika reperfüze edildi; tedavi grubuna reperfüzyon başlangıcında 3000 IU/kg epoetin alfa intraperitoneal olarak uygulandı. Terminal ileum örnekleri Hematoksilen-Eozin ile boyanarak iki bağımsız patolog tarafından kör yöntemle nekroz, ödem ve inflamasyon açısından (Grade 0-4) skorlandı; her hayvan için iki skorun ortalaması nihai skor olarak kullanıldı. İstatistiksel analizde Kruskal-Wallis H testi ve anlamlı parametrelerde Bonferroni düzeltmeli post-hoc Dunn testi uygulandı. Bulgular: Kruskal-Wallis H testi, üç grup arasında tüm parametrelerde ileri düzeyde anlamlı fark ortaya koymuştur (nekroz, ödem, inflamasyon için p<0,001). Bonferroni düzeltmeli post-hoc Dunn testi ile İ/R grubu, sham grubuna kıyasla her parametrede anlamlı biçimde yüksek bulunmuştur (tüm karşılaştırmalar için p_Bonf<0,001). Eritropoietin grubunda nekroz parametresi, İ/R grubuna kıyasla Bonferroni düzeltmeli eşikte istatistiksel olarak anlamlı azalmıştır (p_Bonf=0,026). Ödem ve inflamasyonda ham p değerleri nominal anlamlılık eşiğinin altında olsa da (sırasıyla p=0,040 ve p=0,027), Bonferroni düzeltmesi sonrası anlamlılığa ulaşmamıştır (p_Bonf=0,120 ve p_Bonf=0,080). Sonuç: Reperfüzyon başlangıcında uygulanan tek doz eritropoietin, intestinal iskemi-reperfüzyon hasarında nekroz parametresinde istatistiksel olarak anlamlı koruyucu etki sergilemiştir (p=0,026). Ödem ve inflamasyonda saptanan azalmalar ham p değerinde anlamlı olmakla birlikte, konservatif Bonferroni düzeltmesi sonrası istatistiksel anlamlılığa ulaşmamıştır. Eritropoietin, özellikle geri dönüşsüz hücresel hasar (nekroz) bileşeni üzerinde umut verici bir sitoprotektif ajan olarak değerlendirilmekte; klinik pratiğe aktarılabilmesi için farklı doz ve zamanlamaları içeren ileri deneysel çalışmalara ihtiyaç duyulmaktadır. Anahtar Kelimeler: Eritropoietin, Mezenterik iskemi, İskemi-reperfüzyon hasarı, İntestinal mukoza, Sitoproteksiyon, Sıçan

makaleler.baslik: Outcomes of polyglycolic acid sheet shielding after gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection in patients receiving anticoagulants or dual antiplatelet therapy: a prospective multicenter study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Antikoagülan Alanlarda Gastrik ESD Sonrası PGA Kalkanı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Antikoagülan veya DAPT alan 125 hastada gastrik ESD sonrası gecikmiş kanamayı önlemede PGA örtüsü ve fibrin yapıştırıcı değerlendirildi. Gecikmiş kanama %10,4 oranında görüldü ve önceden belirlenen %15'lik eşik değeri karşılamadı (p=0,09).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Delayed bleeding after gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) remains a significant clinical complication, particularly in patients receiving anticoagulants/ dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, effective preventive measures are not established and the efficacy of endoscopic shielding using polyglycolic acid (PGA) sheets with fibrin glue in this high-risk population remains unclear. This study prospectively evaluated the efficacy of PGA sheets and fibrin glue shielding in preventing delayed bleeding after gastric ESD in patients receiving anticoagulants/ DAPT.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, single-arm confirmatory study was conducted at 13 Japanese institutions. Patients with gastric neoplasms who underwent ESD while receiving anticoagulants/DAPT were enrolled. Following standard ESD and prophylactic coagulation, PGA sheets and fibrin glue were applied to the ulcer beds. The primary endpoint was delayed bleeding within 28 days. Secondary endpoints included late delayed bleeding, transfusion, emergency endoscopy, and thromboembolic events.
RESULTS: We included 125 patients in this study. Delayed bleeding occurred in 13 (10.4%) patients (95% confidence interval: 5.7-17.1%), which did not meet the pre-specified threshold of 15% (p = 0.09), and late delayed bleeding occurred in 7.2%. Bleeding rates were higher in DAPT (28.6%) than in anticoagulant users (9.3%). Blood transfusion was required in 5.6% of the patients, and thromboembolic events occurred in 0.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: The prespecified efficacy threshold was not met. Delayed bleeding occurred in 10.4% of patients receiving anticoagulants or DAPT. Further controlled studies are needed to determine whether PGA shielding provides clinical benefit in this high-risk population.

makaleler.baslik: Endoscopic Balloon Dilation Versus Endoscopic Stricturotomy for Short Crohn's Disease Strictures: The BEST-CD Randomized Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kısa Crohn Darlıklarında Endoskopik Dilatasyon ve Strikturotomi Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 106 hastanın dahil olduğu RCT'de, kısa Crohn darlıklarında endoskopik strikturotomi, 1 yılda endoskopik balon dilatasyonuna kıyasla daha düşük klinik nüks (%30,1'e karşı %54,7; p=0,01) ve yeniden girişim oranları (%24,5'e karşı %49,1; p=0,01) ile ilişkili bulunmuştur.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic balloon dilation (EBD) is the standard therapy for Crohn's disease (CD) strictures but is limited by recurrence and reinterventions. Randomized comparative data on endoscopic stricturotomy (ES) vs EBD are lacking.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, adults (18-65 years) with symptomatic CD and short (<3 cm) strictures accessible by standard endoscopy were randomly assigned (1:1) to EBD or ES. The primary outcome was clinical recurrence at 1 year. Secondary outcomes at 1 year included reintervention, surgery, and stricture-related emergency visits and hospitalisation; safety was assessed at 30 days. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 12 months.
RESULTS: Of 164 patients screened, 106 were randomised (EBD n=53; ES n=53). In the intention-to-treat population, clinical recurrence at 1 year was lower with ES than EBD (30.1% vs 54.7%; p=0·01), as were reintervention (24.5% vs 49.1%; p=0·01), emergency visits (18.9% vs 50.9%; p=0·001), and hospitalisations (15.1% vs 34%; p=0·02). Surgery did not differ significantly (1.9% vs 11.3%; p=0·11). In 12-month time-to-event analyses, EBD was associated with higher hazards of clinical recurrence (HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.23-4.18) and reintervention (HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.23-4.68), with consistent findings for emergency visits and hospitalisation. Adverse events were similar (13·2% vs 22.6%; p=0·30).
CONCLUSION: ES was associated with lower 1-year clinical recurrence and reintervention than EBD for short CD strictures. These findings support ES as a promising endoscopic strategy in expert centres and warrant validation in multicentre studies. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05521867).

makaleler.baslik: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Sedasyonsuz EGD'de Simetikon ve N-Asetilsistein İçeren Lidokain Buzlu Çubuk
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 374 hastada yapılan prospektif RCT'de, lidokain buzlu çubuğa simetikon ve N-asetilsistein eklenmesi, sedasyonsuz EGD sırasında mukozal görünürlüğü belirgin şekilde artırmış ve işlem süresini kısaltmıştır (10,87 dakikaya karşı 12,75 dakika; p<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).
RESULTS: All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up.

makaleler.baslik: Real-time Voice-Guided Artificial Intelligence Improves Biliopancreatic Endosonography Quality: A Randomized Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Gerçek Zamanlı Yapay Zeka ile Biliyopankreatik EUS Kalitesinin Artırılması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 266 hastada yapılan RCT'de, sesli yönlendirmeli gerçek zamanlı yapay zeka navigasyon sistemi (EUS-GUIDEQ), standart EUS'a kıyasla istasyon tamlığını artırmış (median 1,00'e karşı 0,81; p<0,001) ancak işlem süresini uzatmıştır (12,70 dakikaya karşı 10,55 dakika; p<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) quality is operator-dependent, and adherence to guideline-recommended multi-station biliopancreatic scanning remains suboptimal. We developed a device (named EUS-GUIDEQ), an artificial intelligence (AI)-based real-time EUS navigation and quality-control system providing station recognition, voice-guided prompts, and quantitative completeness feedback. We evaluated its performance and clinical utility.
METHODS: EUS-GUIDEQ was developed from 27,072 annotated biliopancreatic EUS images obtained from 189 patients and validated on independent datasets consisting of 1,500 internal images and 2,062 multicenter external images. We then conducted a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial (1:1) comparing AI-assisted versus standard EUS. The primary endpoint was completeness of standardized scanning stations. Secondary endpoints included station-level and landmarks completeness, procedure duration (observation time excluding additional interventions), and adverse events. Outcomes were adjudicated by blinded expert review of recorded videos.
RESULTS: Station-classification model achieved accuracies of 94.2% internally and 78.8% externally. Between December 12, 2023, and May 16, 2025, 266 patients were analyzed (AI-assisted n=132; control n=134). Overall station completeness was higher with EUS-GUIDEQ assistance (median [IQR] 1.00 [0.94-1.00] vs 0.81 [0.75-0.88]; P<0.001), with benefit observed across participating endoscopists. Completeness was higher for most anatomical landmarks in nominal comparisons. Procedure time was longer with AI assistance (12.70±3.23 vs 10.55±3.62 min; P<0.001). No serious procedure-related adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In a randomized trial, voice-guided real-time AI navigation improved guideline-level biliopancreatic EUS process quality, as measured by station completeness, but increased procedure time. Multicenter, multi-vendor prospective validation is warranted.

makaleler.baslik: Ergonomics in gastrointestinal endoscopy ‒ A position statement of the Spanish Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Gastrointestinal Endoskopide Ergonomi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: İspanyol Gastrointestinal Endoskopi Derneği (SEED) anketinde hekimlerin %69,1'i endoskopi kaynaklı kas-iskelet sistemi rahatsızlığı bildirmiştir. Delphi konsensusu ile endoskopide ergonomi eğitimi, mikro molalar ve doğru monitor/masa pozisyonu gibi sekiz öneri geliştirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet: Endoscopy involves prolonged standing, static postures, repetitive hand and wrist movements, sustained force on the controls, manual torque of the insertion tube and, during fluoroscopic procedures, the additional load imposed by radiation protection equipment. In a survey conducted by the Spanish Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (SEED), 69.1% of responding physicians reported discomfort or injury associated with endoscopic practice that had led to medication use, medical consultation or sick leave. The most frequently affected regions were the back/neck (50.8%), wrists/hands (35.0%) and shoulders (8.5%). The SEED Ergonomics Committee was established and developed eight statements, all of which reached Delphi consensus (agreement ranging from 80.9% to 100%): 1. SEED recommends incorporating structured education in ergonomics (before, during and after procedures) into endoscopy training programmes and continuing professional development. 2. SEED recommends taking microbreaks during procedures and scheduled breaks during endoscopy sessions. 3. Alternate endoscopic activity with other tasks and avoid concentrating prolonged or physically demanding procedures within a single working day, where organisational arrangements and staffing permit. 4. Position the monitor directly in front of the operator and approximately 15-30° below eye level to promote a neutral neck posture and avoid sustained flexion or hyperextension. 5. Adjust the height of the procedure bed or table to promote a neutral posture during endoscopy, with the working area approximately at or slightly below elbow level and the elbows flexed at approximately 90°. 6. Introduce an ergonomic check or checklist before each procedure to assess posture, bed and monitor height, pedal positioning and equipment accessibility. 7. Consider technological adaptations of the endoscope and ergonomic support devices for endoscopists with musculoskeletal symptoms or difficulty adapting to standard equipment, as part of an individualised approach to prevention or rehabilitation. 8. Apply comprehensive ergonomic principles during fluoroscopic procedures, including optimisation of posture and distance from the radiation emitter, appropriate use of radiation protection measures and balanced distribution of the load imposed by protective equipment.

turk.baslik: Surgeons' preferences in the management of recurrence after laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: A nationwide survey.
turk.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik İnguinal Herni Nüksünde Cerrah Tercihleri
turk.kisa_ozet: 179 cerrahın katıldığı ulusal ankette, laparoskopik herni onarımı hacmi yüksek olan cerrahların erken ve geç nükslerde yeniden laparoskopik posterior yaklaşımı daha sık tercih ettiği saptanmıştır (p<0,05). Katılımcıların çoğunluğu nüks onarımında standart eğitim eksikliği bildermiştir.
turk.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate contemporary surgical approaches and decision-making patterns of general surgeons in the management of recurrent inguinal hernia following laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair (LIHR), with particular emphasis on recurrence timing, surgeon experience, and annual laparoscopic case volume.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The questionnaire consisted of 26 items, including both multiple-choice and short-answer questions, and was designed to assess demographic characteristics, surgical experience, preferred surgical techniques, preoperative evaluation strategies, and management approaches for recurrent inguinal hernia following LIHR. Recurrences were classified as early (≤2 years) or late (>2 years) based on the postoperative time interval.
RESULTS: A total of 179 surgeons participated in the survey. Most respondents were male and had ≤10 years of surgical experience. Surgeons with higher annual laparoscopic hernia repair volumes were significantly more likely to prefer re-laparoscopic posterior approaches for both early and late recurrences, whereas surgeons with lower case volumes predominantly favored open anterior repair techniques (p<0.05). Surgical preferences also varied in female patients and according to the initial repair technique (transabdominal preperitoneal or total extraperitoneal). Nearly two-thirds of participants reported insufficient or only partially sufficient training in recurrent hernia repair, while the majority strongly agreed on the need for national or international clinical guidelines.
CONCLUSION: Surgeon experience and annual laparoscopic case volume significantly influence the management of recurrent inguinal hernia following LIHR. As laparoscopic expertise increases, re-laparoscopic approaches are more frequently adopted. These findings highlight the need for standardized training programs and evidence-based guidelines to optimize the management of recurrent inguinal hernia after laparoscopic repair.

tez.baslik: Endoskopik hiatal morfolojinin yapay zeka algoritması kullanılarak değerlendirilmesi
tez.baslik_tr: Endoskopik Hiatal Morfolojinin Yapay Zeka ile Değerlendirilmesi
tez.kisa_ozet: 9094 endoskopik retrovert hiatus görüntüsü retrospektif olarak değerlendirilmiş ve EfficientNet tabanlı derin öğrenme modeli, klinik kritik evre 4 olgularda yüksek duyarlılık (%91,3) ve özgüllük (%99,3) göstermiştir.
tez.ozet: Amaç: Endoskopi arşivindeki retrovert hiatus görüntü kayıtları kullanılarak, normal (mide-yemek borusu bölgesinin diyafram kası içindeki yerleşim yerinin endoskopik skopu yeterli sardığı) görüntü ile anormal (mide-yemek borusu bölgesinin diyafram kası içindeki yerleşim yerinin endoskopik skopu yeterli sarmadığı) görüntü arasında ayırım yapabilen ve hiatal morfolojiyi evreleyebilen derin öğrenme tabanlı bir yapay zeka algoritması geliştirmek. Gereç ve Yöntem: 01.01.2019 ile 31.12.2023 tarihleri arasındaki Kütahya Sağlık Bilimleri Üniversitesi Evliya Çelebi Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi Kliniği Endoskopi Ünitesinde elde edilen toplam 9094 retrovert hiatus görüntüsü retrospektif olarak değerlendirilmiştir. Görüntüler, The American Foregut Society (AFS) Hiatus Sınıflamasına göre evre 1–4 arasında etiketlenmiştir. Tüm görüntülerde, sınıf etiketlemesine ek olarak, gastroözofageal bileşke ve hiatal bölgeyi içeren ilgili anatomik alanlar manuel olarak çerçeve içine alınarak işaretlenmiştir. Veri seti %70-%30 gibi oranlar dikkate alınarak eğitim veri kümesi-test veri kümesi şeklinde iki bölüme ayrılmıştır. Sınıflama modellerinin genelleştirilmesi için çapraz doğrulama yapılmıştır. EfficientNet ve DenseNet tabanlı derin öğrenme modelleri, öğrenme aktarımı yaklaşımı kullanılarak eğitilmiştir. Model performansı doğruluk, dengeli doğruluk, duyarlılık, kesinlik, F1 skoru, ROC-AUC ve karmaşıklık matrisi metrikleri ile değerlendirilmiştir. Ayrıca Grad-CAM yöntemi kullanılarak modellerin karar verme süreçleri görselleştirilmiştir. Bulgular: EfficientNet modeli, tüm evrelerde dengeli ve yüksek performans göstermiştir. Özellikle klinik açıdan kritik olan evre 4 olgularında yüksek duyarlılık (%91,3) ve özgüllük (%99,3) değerleri elde edilmiştir. DenseNet modelinde ise belirgin çoğunluk sınıf yanlılığı gözlenmiş ve ara evrelerin ayırt edilmesinde performans düşüklüğü saptanmıştır. Grad-CAM analizleri, EfficientNet modelinin tahminlerini gastroözofageal bileşke çevresindeki anatomik olarak anlamlı bölgelere dayandırdığını göstermiştir. Sonuçlar: Bu çalışma, endoskopik hiatal morfolojinin derin öğrenme algoritmaları ile güvenilir ve yorumlanabilir biçimde sınıflandırılabileceğini göstermektedir. Özellikle EfficientNet tabanlı model, hiatal herni evrelemesinde klinik karar destek sistemi olarak kullanılmaya adaydır. Anahtar Kelimeler: Hiatal Herni, Endoskopi, Yapay Zeka, Derin Öğrenme, Klinik Karar Destek Sistemi

makaleler.baslik: Robotic Surgical Curricula Implementation Strategies for Trainees: A Systematic Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Robotik Cerrahi Müfredat Uygulama Stratejileri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 30 RAS eğitim müfredatını inceleyen sistematik derlemede, ana uygulama stratejilerinin geliştirilmiş erişim, korumalı süre ve zorunlu eğitim olduğu bildirilmiştir. Kanıt kalitesi düşük bulunmuştur.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Numerous curricula have been developed in response to the increasing use of robotic-assisted surgery (RAS). Less work has been done on strategies for implementation of RAS training into existing surgical training structures. We conducted a systematic review of implementation strategies across an international range of postgraduate training curricula.
METHODS: A systematic review of RAS curricula evidence and teaching was conducted on the platforms MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO in February 2024, updated in June 2025. Screening 10000 references using the population, intervention, comparator, outcomes framework for eligibility: surgical trainees, implemented curricula and educational interventions, reporting on curricula success or patient outcomes identified 33 studies reporting on 30 RAS educational interventions. Data were extracted and analyzed thematically, with NVivo 14 using Kern et al.'s curricula implementation framework: People, Time, Facilities, Funding, Administration, and Introduction. Quality was assessed using the Modified Medical Education Research Study Quality Instrument criteria (PROSPERO CRD42024566778).
RESULTS: Implementation strategies reported in the 33 publications were improved access, protected time, and mandatory training. The reporting on implementation methods was variable, unstructured, and anecdotal. The RAS educators, essential to curriculum success, may need specific training. For trainee progress, tracking simulator scores, operative steps, percentage of active time, and operative scores were important measures.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence is of low quality. When implementing a RAS curriculum, the key areas for successful implementation are the RAS surgical educators, a relevant motivating simulation curriculum, RAS exposure, and performance tracking. Protected training time and good access to simulation facilities may also support trainees in preclinical training.

makaleler.baslik: Determining the sweet spot for rural hospital engagement in general surgery training.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Genel Cerrahi Eğitiminde Kırsal Hastane Entegrasyonu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 6 eyaletteki kırsal hastane verileri ile yapılan kesitsel çalışmada, 467 kırsal hastanenin GME-naif olduğu saptanmıştır. CMS kriterlerine göre 5 ila 8 hastane tam zamanlı asistan barındırabilirken, 17 ila 26 hastane eğitim süresinin %50'sinden fazlasını karşılamıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
PURPOSE: The shortage of rural general surgeons in the U.S. limits access to surgical care for rural communities. Rural training opportunities prepare surgery residents for rural practice and offer a solution to this workforce crisis. Rural-focused graduate medical education (GME) funding has had limited uptake for general surgery. This study sought to determine whether procedure volume at rural hospitals might limit training opportunities.
METHOD: The authors performed a cross-sectional study of fiscal year 2019 inpatient discharge data for a multi-state cohort of inpatient discharges in Arizona, California, Iowa, North Carolina, Vermont and Wisconsin. All rural hospitals not associated with a general surgery training program or currently receiving Federal GME funding were included. Rurality was defined using both Federal Office of Rural Health Policy (FORHP) and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) criteria. The authors estimated the ability of rural hospitals to "host" general surgery residents as a function of the inpatient surgical volume at the hospital and resident case log requirements. Potential residents were classified as full (100% of procedure volume), or 51%, 30% or 20% of procedural volume.
RESULTS: Of the rural hospitals studied in six states, 467 were both GME-naïve and unaffiliated with a general surgery program. Among CMS and FORHP rural hospitals, 5-8 could host a full-time resident for 100% of the general surgery residency training time, 17-26 met criteria for greater than 50% of training time and 40-55 for at least 20% of training time.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals that few rural hospitals can establish general surgery residencies that meet current eligibility for Medicare GME financing of Rural Track Programs. Hosting rural rotations and partnering with hospitals for training offer substantial potential for rural general surgery GME expansion among rural hospitals.

makaleler.baslik: Virtual reality surgical simulator training of residents and early-career surgeons for pedicle screw placement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Pedikül Vida Yerleştirme İçin VR Simülatör Eğitimi: Meta-Analiz
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 6 adet RCT'yi içeren bu meta-analizde, VR simülasyon eğitimi alan asistan ve erken kariyer cerrahların optimal pedikül vida yerleştirme oranı geleneksel eğitime göre anlamlı derecede yüksek bulundu (RR 1,36; %95 CI 1,15-1,61). Ayrıca VR eğitimi, tüm kortikal ihlal derecelerinde tutarlı azalma ve daha yüksek genel prosedürel başarı sağladı (RR 1,17; %95 CI 1,04-1,32).
makaleler.ozet:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of Virtual reality (VR) simulation training compared with traditional teaching methods for residents and early-career surgeons training in pedicle screw insertion.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing VR simulator training with traditional training approaches for pedicle screw placement in residents and early-career surgeons were included. A random-effects model was applied to pool outcomes, with treatment effects expressed as mean differences or risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: A total of six RCTs were included, with 54 trainees and 457 screws inserted in each study group. Pooled analyses demonstrated that residents and early-career surgeons trained with VR simulation achieved a significantly higher rate of optimal (Grade I) pedicle screw placement than those receiving conventional training (RR 1.36; 95% CI 1.15 to 1.61). Conversely, VR training was associated with significantly lower rates of Grade II (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.85), Grade III (RR 0.07; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.30), and Grade IV screw placements (RR 0.16; 95% CI 0.03 to 0.90), indicating consistent reductions across all severities of cortical breach. Overall procedural success was significantly higher in the VR group (RR 1.17; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.32). Furthermore, VR-trained residents and early-career surgeons demonstrated shorter screw penetration distances and fewer displaced screws per resident.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that VR simulation training significantly enhances accuracy and safety-related outcomes in resident and early-career surgeons' pedicle screw placement training.

makaleler.baslik: Dissecting the role of anatomy in guidance for intraoperative clinical reasoning.
makaleler.baslik_tr: İntraoperatif klinik akıl yürütmede anatominin rolü
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Konstrüktivist temellendirilmiş teori yaklaşımı kullanılan bu çalışmada, 3 Kanada akademik hastanesinde 6 cerrah ve 8 asistanla yapılan gözlemler ve mülakatlar analiz edilmiştir. Anatomi temelli rehberlik etkileşimleri için 3 tema geliştirilmiş olup, anatominin paylaşılan iletişim aracı olarak işlev gördüğü ve klinik akıl yürütme süreçlerini görünür kıldığı gösterilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Anatomy is indispensable to surgical expertise, yet surgical residents often struggle to translate anatomical knowledge into safe and efficient operative decisions. This disconnect can contribute to errors, hesitation and missed opportunities for autonomy. Despite the centrality of anatomy in surgical practice, research has rarely examined how surgeons draw on anatomical knowledge in their clinical reasoning and how residents learn to do so under real operative pressures. This blind spot means that opportunities to deliberately cultivate reasoning skills anchored in anatomy may be overlooked.
METHOD: A constructivist grounded theory approach was used to analyse observational and interview data to explore the role of anatomy in interactions between surgeons and residents to guide intraoperative clinical reasoning. Participants included general surgery consultants and residents at three Canadian academic hospitals. Field notes were documented by observing participants throughout six operative days, capturing 16 individual operations. Follow-up semi-structured interviews were completed with six surgeons and eight residents.
RESULTS: Three themes representing different guidance interactions were developed: establishing trust, aligning understanding throughout operative progress and teaching future decision-making. Using these themes, a model of anatomy-based guidance interactions was created showing how anatomy functions as a shared communication tool, serves as common landmarks for operative progress and helps make clinical reasoning processes explicit.
CONCLUSIONS: The power of explicitly verbalising anatomy in surgical guidance interactions lies in making tacit reasoning processes accessible. Anatomy facilitated bilateral communication that created and maintained a shared mental model for residents and surgeons throughout an operation, allowing surgeons to understand a resident's thinking and enabling residents to see how surgeons connected foundational knowledge to surgical decision-making. Through explicit use of anatomy-based guidance, these interactions simultaneously scaffolded residents' in-the-moment decision-making and developed their clinical reasoning for future operations.

makaleler.baslik: Out in the Match: Navigating Identity and Psychological Safety for LGBTQ+ General Surgery Applicants.
makaleler.baslik_tr: LGBTQ+ Genel Cerrahi Adaylarının Psikolojik Güvenliği
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 17 katılımcı ile yapılan nitel çalışmada, ortalama yaş 30,7±1,8 yıl olup katılımcıların %52,9'u erkek ve %76,5'i Beyaz olarak bulunmuştur. Adayların psikolojik güvenliği değerlendirmek için zamansal micro-signal ve coğrafi konumu kullandığı saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To explore LGBTQ+ general surgery resident experiences during the Match process.
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: General surgery (GS) applicants negotiate the residency match process through the lens of their identities, but little is known about LGBTQ+ applicant experiences. This study explored how current LGBTQ+-GS residents navigated their identity and evaluated programs for psychological safety and belonging during the Match.
METHODS: This qualitative study utilized semistructured interviews with current US LGBTQ+-GS residents recruited using purposive and snowball sampling from Oct to Dec 2025. Interviews focused on LGBTQ+ identity, experiences throughout medical school, recruitment, and residency, and how psychological safety was assessed. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using a deductive-inductive approach to identify themes.
RESULTS: Of 17 participants, mean age was 30.7±1.8 years, and most identified as male (52.9%) and White (76.5%). Five themes were identified: (1) Participants strategically disclosed identity: disclosing as a "litmus test" to filter for identity-affirming programs or concealing identity in fear "that's the reason why I don't get ranked." (2) Participants relied on subtle micro-signals to indicate psychological safety (eg, pronouns, pride symbols). (3) Participants scrutinized the manner and tone of responses to LGBTQ+-related questions in addition to the content. (4) Representation of LGBTQ+ residents/faculty reduced belonging uncertainty. (5) Participants "used geography as a proxy for acceptance," weighing regional sociopolitical climates when assessing their potential to thrive.
CONCLUSIONS: LGBTQ+ trainees assessed a variety of micro- and macro-signals to evaluate residency programs. Residency programs can design their programs around these signals to enhance recruitment of LGBTQ+-GS applicants.

makaleler.baslik: Patient-Specific Implant Design: Current Evidence for Artificial Intelligence, Imaging and Computational Planning-A Systematic Review of the Biomedical-Indexed Literature.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Hastaya Özel İmplant Tasarımında Yapay Zeka ve Görüntüleme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Hastaya özel implantların yapay zeka ve hesaplamalı planlama süreçlerini inceleyen 639 çalışmalık derlemede, implantların sanal plandan daha az saptığı (standardize ortalama fark -1,21; %95 CI -1,69 - -0,74) ve revizyon oranının daha düşük olduğu (risk oranı 0,28; %95 CI 0,11 - 0,72) bulundu.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Patient-specific skeletal implants are designed through a pipeline of imaging, computational planning and, increasingly, artificial intelligence. Each pillar has its own validation literature, but no review has asked what evidence supports each one in implant design itself. We mapped that evidence from the biomedical-indexed literature in this paper.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted under a protocol committed before retrieval (PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, SWiM). MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Crossref and OpenAlex were searched on 2 and 3 September 2026 for primary studies from 2015 onwards applying artificial intelligence, an evaluated imaging pipeline or computational planning to an implant whose geometry derives from the individual patient's anatomy. Engineering indexes were unavailable, so this review maps biomedical-indexed literature, and a bounded probe was used to estimate what that omits. Two artificial intelligence screeners from different vendors screened every record; every clinical study was appraised twice, independently, by assessors from different vendors. Claims about validation quality are reported on the studies read in full. All screening, charting and appraisals were machine-performed and no human-verified subsample exists.
RESULTS: Of 5059 records, 639 studies were included: 373 technical studies, 179 clinical series, 75 comparative studies and 12 randomised trials. Computational planning was applied in 601, an evaluated imaging step in 219 and artificial intelligence in 36. Randomised evidence came from 12 small trials, 10 of them craniomaxillofacial, which evaluated the delivered implant rather than the planning method; virtual surgical planning was used in 11 of them. When restricting to the four studies that measure deviation from the virtual plan, with smaller meaning better, patient-specific implants deviated less from the plan (standardised mean difference -1.21, 95% CI -1.69 to -0.74). Revision or removal was less frequent (3 of 135 against 25 of 149; risk ratio 0.28, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.72); operative time, complications and infection gave intervals compatible with a difference either way. No randomised trial was at low risk of bias, and 69 of 75 comparative studies were at serious risk, mostly of unadjusted confounding, so all estimates are of very low certainty. Among technical studies read in full, independent validation material was used in fewer than half, and files were shared in about one in fourteen. Of 36 artificial intelligence studies, 4 were evaluated on independent data, 2 were used for a real patient, none were clinically comparative, and 8 of 17 cranial studies relied on AutoImplant family benchmarks.
CONCLUSIONS: The design pipeline is unequally validated: planning has clinical evidence concentrated in one region, computational methods are widely applied but rarely validated independently or shared, and artificial intelligence has benchmark evidence for cranial defect completion and little else. Outcome studies of patient-specific implants should be read as evidence about whole pipelines, and future studies should evaluate the components.

makaleler.baslik: Automation of Living Clinical Practice Guideline Development: Scoping Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Klinik Pratik Kılavuz Geliştirmenin Otomasyonu: Kapsam İncelemesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Klinik pratik kılavuz geliştirmeyi otomatikleştiren hesaplama yöntemlerini inceleyen 47 çalışmanın dahil olduğu kapsam incelemesinde, retrieval ve extraction aşamalarında başarı gösterilirken uçtan uca canlı kılavuz hatları için kanıtların sınırlı olduğu görüldü.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) translate research evidence into actionable recommendations, but their development faces mounting challenges. With dozens of trials and systematic reviews published daily, the traditional 18- to 24-month development cycle struggles to incorporate emerging evidence, and manual screening, synthesis, and quality assessment consume thousands of person-hours per guideline. The resulting knowledge translation pipeline is slow, inconsistent, and quickly outdated.
OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to chart the computational methods empirically tested for automating CPG development, the tasks they address, and their evaluation measures, and to map where that evidence is concentrated and where it is absent for living guidelines.
METHODS: The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidance. We searched PubMed and Scopus for studies published between January 2001 and December 2025, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching. Eligible studies used automated methods for a guideline development task, reported original research with empirical testing, and gave sufficient methodological detail. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Findings were charted across 4 pillars: retrieval, extraction, encoding, and evaluation.
RESULTS: A total of 47 studies met eligibility criteria, spanning 2001 to 2025, with a marked increase after 2015 and a surge in large language model (LLM) work in 2024-2025. Pillar counts (nonexclusive) were as follows: retrieval, 6; extraction, 15; encoding, 26; and evaluation, 17. In retrieval pillar, query expansion achieved 80% recall, while semantic search tools traded recall for specificity (98%). In extraction, rule-based natural language processing achieved an F-measure of 81.96% for structured clinical actions and 71.75% for patient states, and hybrid ontology methods covered 86% of eligibility criteria; LLMs performed well on structured fields but degraded on interpretive content. In encoding, approaches progressed from formalisms such as Guideline Interchange Format version 3 (GLIF3) and guideline elements model toward Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)-based representation; semiautomated tools assisted guideline encoding, and logic verification detected inconsistencies and coverage gaps missed by human reviewers. In evaluation, LLM appraisers assigned higher Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) scores than human appraisers, by a mean difference of 12.5% in one study (95% limits of agreement -30.6% to 55.5%; intraclass correlation coefficient 0.753) and by 22 to 60 percentage points across domains in another.
CONCLUSIONS: Automation shows promise for bounded, well-structured guideline development tasks, while robust evidence for end-to-end, production-scale living guideline pipelines remains limited. No included study demonstrated a validated pipeline connecting all 4 pillars in an operating guideline program, and evidence on clinical safety, workflow integration, and cost-effectiveness is largely absent. Realizing living guidelines will require interoperability standards such as FHIR, and evaluation in real guideline production rather than retrospective benchmarks.

makaleler.baslik: Clinical Safety Thresholds and Decision Risks of Search-Augmented Large Language Models in Acute Pancreatitis: A Guideline-Anchored Evaluation for Surgical Practice.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Akut Pankreatitte Arama Destekli LLM'lerin Klinik Güvenliği
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2025 IAP/APA akut pankreatit kılavuzuna dayalı 27 klinik senaryoda ChatGPT-5.3 ve Gemini 3.0 Flash modellerinin doğruluk ve güvenlik eşikleri değerlendirildi. Gemini ortalama completeness skoru ChatGPT'den yüksek bulundu (4,33'e karşı 4,33; p=0,042), ancak ölümcül hatalar ve yüksek akademik okuma düzeyleri özerk kullanımı engellemektedir.
makaleler.ozet: BackgroundPatients and clinicians increasingly consult search-augmented Large Language Models (LLMs) for point-of-care decision support. However, their safety thresholds against newly revised guidelines remain unverified. This study established a safety baseline evaluating the clinical accuracy, completeness, quality, and readability of ChatGPT-5.3 and Gemini 3.0 Flash anchored to the 2025 IAP/APA acute pancreatitis guidelines.MethodsTwenty-seven consensus-derived clinical scenarios spanning diagnosis, management, intervention, and discharge were queried using zero-shot prompts. Three blinded general surgeons evaluated outputs using 5-point Likert scales for accuracy, completeness, and Global Quality Score (GQS), alongside binary error metrics. Readability was quantified via FRES, FKGL, and SMOG indices. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Intraclass Correlation Coefficients (ICC).ResultsGemini demonstrated significantly higher completeness than ChatGPT (median [IQR]: 4.33 [4.33-4.67] vs 4.33 [4.00-4.33]; corrected P = .042); Global Quality Scores did not differ significantly (corrected P = .231). Clinical accuracy was comparable (P = .217). Response-level hallucination rates were similar (ChatGPT: 25.9% vs Gemini: 22.2%; P = 1.000). One fatal error (advocating premature necrosectomy) occurred in the Gemini cohort (3.7%). High-score concentration induced a ceiling effect, attenuating ICC values. Both models operated at a 12th-grade reading level. ChatGPT's quality correlated positively with word count (ρ = 0.419, P < .05), whereas Gemini maintained volume-independent density.ConclusionBoth LLMs display strong baseline fidelity to the 2025 IAP/APA guidelines. However, persistent critical errors and high academic reading levels preclude autonomous deployment. Establishing this safety floor is an indispensable prerequisite for human-in-the-loop usability trials, positioning LLMs strictly as supervised clinical co-pilots.

makaleler.baslik: Efficacy and implementation of augmented reality in healthcare: a scoping review in randomized controlled trials.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Sağlıkta Artırılmış Gerçekliğin Etkinliği ve Uygulanması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Sağlık hizmetlerinde artırılmış gerçeklik (AR) müdahalelerini içeren 25 RCT'nin analiz edildiği incelemede, AR'ın cerrahi hassasiyeti artırdığı ve perioperatif kaygıyı azalttığı gösterildi. Ancak teknik kısıtlamalar, fizyolojik yan etkiler ve yüksek maliyetler rutin entegrasyonu engellemektedir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Despite medical advances, significant challenges in routine practice persist, including diagnostic variability from traditional two-dimensional (2D) imaging, surgical risks due to anatomical uncertainty, and poor patient comprehension that contributes to perioperative anxiety. Augmented Reality (AR) offers a solution by overlaying three-dimensional (3D) digital information onto the real-world environment, providing real-time guidance to address these clinical gaps. However, while AR's clinical efficacy is increasingly proven, its practical integration into standard clinical workflows remains fragmented.
OBJECTIVE: This study presents a scoping review restricted to RCT-level evidence to systematically map the scope, distinct clinical capabilities, implementation limitations, and ethical frameworks of AR-based healthcare systems.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed and Embase to identify randomized controlled trials involving AR interventions in healthcare. Methodological quality was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. A total of 25 Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) were analyzed and categorized based on clinical domains (education, diagnosis, intervention, and rehabilitation) and their functional roles (delivering or assisting).
RESULTS: AR was associated with improvements in surgical precision, reductions in perioperative anxiety and better functional outcomes in rehabilitation. In education, AR 3D models fostered patient engagement and shared decision-making. However, widespread adoption is impeded by technical constraints, physiological side effects like cybersickness, high initial costs, and inherent methodological difficulties in blinding.
CONCLUSIONS: While AR demonstrates distinct capabilities to enhance clinical interventions and empower patient care, technical, logistical, and ethical hurdles persist. Future research must prioritize seamless interoperability with Electronic Health Records (EHR), integration with Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision support, robust health data architectures, and optimized human-computer interaction (HCI) factor design to prevent exacerbating the socioeconomic digital divide.

makaleler.baslik: Before Sepsis Strikes: Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Postoperative Sepsis and Sepsis-Related Complications After Major Abdominal Surgery-A Systematic Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Batın Cerrahisi Sonrası Sepsis için Yapay Zeka ile Erken Tahmin
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Majör batın cerrahisi sonrası sepsis ve enfeksiyon komplikasyonlarını tahmin eden AI/ML modellerinin incelendiği 45 çalışmalık derlemede, umut vadeden performanslara rağmen kanıt kalitesinin yetersiz olduğu ve rutin kullanım için çok merkezli harici validasyon gerektiği belirlendi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative sepsis and related infectious complications remain major causes of morbidity after abdominal surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models may support earlier risk stratification, but their generalizability and clinical readiness remain uncertain.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and CENTRAL from inception to 10 August 2026 for studies developing, validating, or evaluating AI/ML models for postoperative sepsis, postoperative infection/surgical-site infection (SSI), anastomotic leakage, or postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) after major abdominal or general surgery. SSI, anastomotic leakage, and POPF were analyzed as distinct postoperative endpoints and were not treated as proxy definitions of clinical sepsis. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST + AI. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261492111).
RESULTS: Forty-five studies were included: 11 addressed sepsis-related outcomes, including six studies with a primary sepsis-related modeled endpoint whose definitions ranged from consensus Sepsis-3 criteria to coded or SIRS-based definitions and a qSOFA-based proxy; 19 evaluated postoperative infection/SSI; eight anastomotic leakage; five POPF; and two broader postoperative complications. Performance varied according to outcome, surgical population, prediction timing, predictor availability, and validation strategy. Fifteen of 45 studies provided strict temporal, geographic/external-center, or independent-investigator evaluation of the principal model, with variable preservation of performance outside development settings. More complex ML methods did not reliably outperform conventional regression. Explicit calibration analysis was reported in 9/45 studies, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis in 7/45, and no study prospectively evaluated the impact of model-guided care on clinical outcomes. Certainty of evidence was very low for primary postoperative sepsis/septic-shock prediction, low for postoperative infection/SSI, and very low for anastomotic leakage and POPF.
CONCLUSIONS: Although several AI/ML models showed promising predictive performance, the available evidence remains insufficient to support routine use of AI/ML prediction models across major abdominal surgical populations. Future studies should prioritize clearly defined clinical use cases, multicenter external validation, calibration, prospective workflow evaluation, and demonstration of actionable clinical benefit before routine implementation.

tez.baslik: Neoadjuvan kemoterapi alan meme kanseri hastalarında makine öğrenim modelleri kullanılarak patolojik yanıt öngörülebilir mi?
tez.baslik_tr: Meme Kanserinde Neoadjuvan Kemoterapi Yanıtı Tahmini
tez.kisa_ozet: Neoadjuvan kemoterapi alan 214 meme kanseri hastasında yapay zeka modellerinin değerlendirildiği çalışmada, Random Forest algoritması aksiller lenf nodu durumunu %98 doğruluk ve %100 özgüllük ile tahmin ederken, Gaussian Naive Bayes modeli patolojik tam yanıtı 0,936 AUC değeriyle öngördü.
tez.ozet: Giriş ve Amaç: Neoadjuvan kemoterapi, lokal ileri evre meme kanseri tedavisinde standart bir yaklaşım olup, tedaviye verilen patolojik tam yanıtın (pCR) ve aksiller lenf nodu durumunun erken dönemde öngörülmesi, cerrahi planlama ve prognostik değerlendirme açısından kritik öneme sahiptir. Bu çalışmanın amacı, neoadjuvan kemoterapi alan meme kanseri hastalarında klinik, histopatolojik ve radyolojik verileri entegre ederek pCR ve sentinel lenf nodu (SLNB) durumunu tahmin eden makine öğrenimi (ML) modelleri geliştirmek ve performanslarını karşılaştırmaktır. Gereç ve Yöntem: Çalışmaya, Ocak 2014 - Aralık 2024 tarihleri arasında S.B.Ü. İzmir Tepecik Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi Kliniği'nde NAKT sonrası cerrahi tedavi uygulanan 214 kadın hasta dahil edildi. Hastaların demografik verileri, tedavi öncesi ve sonrası ultrasonografik ölçümleri ve histopatolojik özellikleri retrospektif olarak analiz edildi. Veri seti %80 eğitim ve %20 test olarak ayrıldı. pCR ve SLNB sonucunu tahmin etmek için yedi farklı ML algoritması (Random Forest, Gaussian Naive Bayes, SVM, Lojistik Regresyon, kNN, Decision Tree, AdaBoost) eğitildi ve performansları Accuracy, Specificity, F1 Skoru ve ROC-AUC değerleri ile değerlendirildi. Bulgular: Neoadjuvan tedavi sonrası SLNB sonucunun (pozitif/negatif) tahmin edilmesinde Random Forest algoritması, %97.8 F1 skoru, %98 Accuracy, %100 specificity ve 0.973 AUC değeri ile en yüksek performansı göstermiştir. Patolojik tam yanıtın (pCR) öngörülmesinde ise Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB) modeli 0.936 AUC değeri ile en yüksek ayırt etme gücüne ulaşırken; Random Forest modeli %87 F1 skoru, %84 doğruluk ve %92.9 negatif öngörü değeri ile klinik açıdan en dengeli sonuçları vermiştir. Ultrasonografik yanıt verilerinin modellere eklenmesinin, sadece klinik verilerle eğitilen modellere kıyasla tahmin başarısını belirgin şekilde artırdığı saptanmıştır. Sonuç: Bu çalışma, neoadjuvan kemoterapi sonrası cerrahi planlamada en büyük ikilemlerden biri olan "tedavi yanıtının öngörülmesi" sorununa, yapay zeka destekli güçlü ve uygulanabilir bir çözüm sunmaktadır. Çalışmamızda geliştirilen Random Forest modeli, aksiller lenf nodu durumunu %98 doğruluk ve %100 özgüllük ile tahmin ederek, sentinel lenf nodu biyopsisi planlanan hastalarda pozitif-negatif ayrımını yapmada son derece güvenilir bir araç olduğunu kanıtlamıştır. Elde edilen bu bulgu, meme kanseri cerrahisinde "SLNB yapılmaksızın güvenli izlem" stratejisinin klinik olarak uygulanabilirliği açısından güçlü bir kanıt niteliğindedir. Ayrıca, patolojik tam yanıtın öngörülmesinde Gaussian Naive Bayes ve Random Forest modellerinin sergilediği yüksek başarı (AUC: 0.936), tedaviye yanıt vermeyecek hastaların erken dönemde tespit edilmesine ve zaman kaybedilmeden kemoterapi rejiminin değiştirilmesine olanak tanımaktadır. Öte yandan, pCR gelişecek hastaların yüksek doğrulukla belirlenmesi, meme kanseri yönetiminde giderek daha fazla tartışılan "bekle-gör" (watch-and-wait) stratejisinin ve ameliyatsız izlem protokollerinin oluşturulması için sağlam bir zemin hazırlamaktadır. Özellikle ultrasonografik yanıt verilerinin modele entegrasyonu, pahalı genomik testlere gerek kalmadan, mevcut klinik imkanlarla "kişiselleştirilmiş cerrahi" döneminin kapılarını aralamaktadır.
