makaleler.baslik: Negative-Pressure Wound Therapy for Surgical Site Infection Prevention After Elective Open Abdominal Surgery: A Risk-Stratified Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Elektif Açık Batın Cerrahisinde NPWT ile Cerrahi Alan Enfeksiyonu Önleme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Elektif açık batın cerrahisi geçiren 2 639 hastayı içeren 16 RCT'lik meta-analizde, proaktif NPWT genel SSI'yı azaltmıştır (RR 0,60; %95 CI 0,43-0,84; mutlak risk %12,6'ya karşı %19,5). Yüksek gelirli ülkelerdeki çok merkezli çalışmalarda fayda saptanmazken, etki yüksek riskli hastalarda ve düşük gelirli ülkelerde belirgin bulunmuştur.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical-site infection (SSI) is a major source of morbidity after elective open abdominal surgery. Prophylactic negative-pressure wound therapy (NPWT) may reduce SSI, but evidence specific to elective surgery remains limited.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026 for RCTs comparing prophylactic NPWT with standard wound dressing (SWD) in adults undergoing elective open abdominal surgery. The prespecified primary outcome was overall SSI within 30 days. Random-effects (REML) meta-analysis generated risk ratios or mean differences with 95% confidence and prediction intervals; certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2 639 patients) were included; 13 were at low risk of bias. NPWT reduced overall SSI (15 RCTs, 2 134 patients; RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.43-0.84; low certainty; absolute risk 12.6% vs 19.5%, approximately 7% reduction; NNT≈15), superficial SSI (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.98), and seroma (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.86; both high certainty). No significant differences were observed in deep SSI, hematoma, dehiscence, readmission, length of stay, blood loss, operative time, or mortality. Benefit was concentrated in lower-income-country trials and high-risk patients, whereas high-income multicenter trials showed no benefit. Prediction intervals crossed the null, and funnel asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.
CONCLUSIONS: NPWT may reduce overall SSI, superficial SSI, and seroma after elective open abdominal surgery, but effects appear context-dependent and were absent in the highest-quality multicenter trials. Routine use in unselected elective patients is not supported; selective use in high-risk patients may be appropriate, pending confirmatory trials such as PROPEL-2.

makaleler.baslik: Systemic Perioperative Antimicrobial Prophylaxis for Penile Prosthesis Implantation: A Systematic Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Penis Protezi İmplantasyonunda Sistemik Perioperatif Antibiyotik Proflaksisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 11 çalışmayı içeren bir meta-analizde, postoperatif oral antibiyotiklerin enfeksiyon riskini azaltmadığı (pooled odds ratio 1,16; %95 CI 0,89-1,53) ve yüksek doz gentamisinin akut böbrek hasarını artırdığı bulundu. Mevcut kanıtlar üstün bir antibakteriyel rejim belirlemedi ve rutin uzun süreli proflaksiyi desteklemedi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Penile prosthesis infection usually ends in device removal, whereas unnecessarily broad or prolonged prophylaxis causes toxicity and promotes resistance. We assessed whether the systemic perioperative antibacterial or antifungal strategy, dose or duration is associated with infection, infection-related explantation or reoperation or antimicrobial toxicity after primary or revision implantation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 29 August 2026 using two complementary strategies that combined penile-prosthesis terms with antimicrobial-prophylaxis terms and, separately, with infection or explantation terms, without language or date limits, supplemented by related-article expansion and reference-list checking. Comparative primary studies were eligible. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and random-effects models were fitted where independent cohorts reported compatible data.
RESULTS: Of 4947 records, 11 studies were included: one small randomised trial and ten non-randomised studies. The pooled crude frequency of infection or infection-related explantation was 2.50% (95% CI 1.78-3.50; I2 = 89%), a descriptive summary across heterogeneous outcome definitions rather than an estimate of the infection rate under any regimen. Postoperative oral antibiotics were not associated with lower risk (pooled odds ratio 1.16, 95% CI 0.89-1.53). A higher or weight-based gentamicin dose did not reduce infection (pooled odds ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.26-2.18) but was associated with more acute kidney injury in the single study that reported comparative toxicity. Guideline-defined regimens carried higher adjusted risk in two overlapping cohorts and no difference in two others. Antifungal prophylaxis was associated with lower infection in two overlapping analyses but not in a revision-only cohort, an exploratory finding that has not been independently replicated. An explicit dose was reported by only three studies, a numerical duration by four and the interval between administration and incision by none, which limits comparison between regimens, and all non-randomised studies had serious risk of bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence identifies no superior antibacterial regimen and does not support routine prolonged prophylaxis. The exploratory antifungal signal and the preliminary renal safety signal with weight-based gentamicin warrant prospective, standardised multicentre evaluation before either informs routine practice.

makaleler.baslik: Negative Pressure Wound Therapy for Emergency Laparotomy: A Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Acil Laparotomi Sonrası Negatif Basınçlı Yara Tedavisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 8 RCT'yi kapsayan meta-analizde, profilaktik ciNPWT acil laparotomi sonrası SSI (1348 hasta; RR 0,46; p=0,0021), seroma (RR 0,60; p=0,0232) ve yara açılması (RR 0,59; p=0,0238) risklerini düşürdü. Ancak yüksek heterojenlik ve küçük çalışma etkileri nedeniyle seçici kullanım önerilmektedir.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infection (SSI) remains a frequent and clinically important complication after emergency laparotomy. Closed-incision negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been proposed to reduce wound-related complications, but evidence in emergency laparotomy remains mixed.
METHODS: Databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing NPWT with standard dressings after emergency laparotomy were included. The primary outcome was SSI. Secondary outcomes were seroma, wound dehiscence, and length of hospital stay (LOS). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Trial sequential analysis was used to assess the robustness of cumulative evidence. Certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment Development and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Eight randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled SSI estimate favored NPWT (8 studies, n = 1348; RR, 0.46; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.28 to 0.76; P = 0.0021), but heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 71.1%), the largest trial was neutral, and marked asymmetry suggested substantial small study effects. NPWT was also associated with significantly lower risks of seroma (4 studies, n = 1057; RR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.93; P = 0.0232; I2 = 0.0%) and wound dehiscence (7 studies, n = 1287; RR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.93; P = 0.0238; I2 = 32.8%). No significant difference was observed for LOS (7 studies, n = 1287). Certainty of evidence was low for SSI and LOS, and moderate for seroma and wound dehiscence.
CONCLUSIONS: In emergency laparotomy, prophylactic NPWT showed a directionally favorable but uncertain SSI signal and was associated with lower risks of seroma and wound dehiscence, but not shorter hospital stay. The SSI estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial heterogeneity, marked small study effects, and the neutral result of the largest trial. These findings support a selective rather than routine use of NPWT.

makaleler.baslik: Evidence landscape for surgical site infection prevention strategies in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review of literature for intervention development as part of the IMPRESS study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Düşük ve Orta Gelirli Ülkelerde Cerrahi Alan Enfeksiyonunu Önleme Stratejileri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Düşük ve orta gelirli ülkelerde SSI önleme stratejilerini değerlendiren 186 çalışmalık scoping review'da, en sık değerlendirilen müdahaleler arasında tek doz profilaktik antibiyotik ve klorheksidin cilt hazırlığı yer almıştır. Bulgular, perioperatif antimikrobiyal optimizasyonu ile basit enfeksiyon önleme pratiklerinin önemini vurgulamaktadır.
makaleler.ozet:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: Surgical site infections (SSIs) contribute to about 20% of hospital-acquired infections, with an 8–30% incidence in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Hospitals in LMIC settings face limited resources, overcrowding, staff shortages and poor infection control. Evaluating effective, feasible and evidence-based multipronged interventions implementable in LMICs is crucial to guide sustainable SSI prevention strategies and improve outcomes. This scoping review addressed the question: “Which SSI prevention interventions have been evaluated in LMICs?”
DESIGN: The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).
DATA SOURCES: The comprehensive literature search was conducted using three databases: PubMed (National Library of Medicine), Scopus (Elsevier) and Embase (Ovid) during August–September 2024.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Peer-reviewed interventional studies evaluating one or more SSI prevention interventions or intervention bundles were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Title and abstract screening was performed by two independent reviewers in Rayaan according to pre-defined inclusion–exclusion criteria, followed by full-text screening from January to March 2025. Data were extracted from the included studies using a standardised Excel sheet, including absolute reductions in SSI rates.
RESULTS: Of the 8368 studies identified, 5577 remained after de-duplication and underwent title and abstract screening, 245 full-text articles were assessed for full-text review and 186 studies were included in the review. Among the included studies, 101/186 (54.3%) were published between 2020 and 2024, 144/186 (77.4%) were randomised controlled trials and 88 (47.3%) were conducted in India. Overall, 64 SSI prevention interventions were identified, including 13 pre-operative (20.3%), 35 intra-operative (54.7%) and 16 post-operative (25.0%) interventions. The most frequently evaluated interventions were single-dose surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (SAP) for clean/clean-contaminated surgery (32 studies, 17.2%), post-operative restriction of SAP to <24 hours (22, 11.8%), appropriate antibiotic selection (13, 7%) and timing of SAP within 60 min of surgical incision (12, 6.5%), chlorhexidine skin preparation (11, 5.9%) and WHO Surgical Safety Checklist implementation (10, 5.4%). Across the studies, the most consistent reduction in SSI was observed with guideline-concordant perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis, alcohol-based chlorhexidine skin preparation, surgeon hand preparation, limiting operating theatre traffic, negative pressure wound therapy, early postoperative bathing, sterile wound care, patient education and SSI surveillance.
CONCLUSIONS: The review suggests that the evidence from LMICs supports optimisation of perioperative antimicrobial therapy alongside implementation of simple, evidence-based infection prevention practices rather than reliance on prolonged post-operative antibiotic use. Developing context-specific SAP policies and strengthening SSI surveillance and staff education are essential for sustainable improvement. There remains a critical need to design and implement multipronged interventions that are scalable and feasible in LMIC settings.

makaleler.baslik: No superiority of double drains over single drainage after tissue expander-based breast reconstruction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Meme Rekonstrüksiyonu Sonrası Çift Dren ile Tek Dren Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 1350 rekonstrüksiyonu içeren 3 retrospektif çalışmanın meta-analizinde, tek dren ile çift dren stratejileri arasında seroma formasyonu (RR 0,84; p=0,54) veya SSI (RR 1,01; p=0,93) açısından anlamlı fark saptanmadı. Bulgular rutin çift dren kullanımının bir üstünlüğünü göstermedi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The optimal number of drains after postmastectomy tissue expander (TE)-based breast reconstruction remains uncertain. Although double-drain placement may theoretically improve fluid clearance and reduce seroma formation, it may also increase patient discomfort, prolong drain-related morbidity, and potentially increase contamination risk. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared postoperative outcomes between single- and double-drain strategies following TE-based breast reconstruction.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 16, 2026. Comparative studies evaluating single versus double drains after postmastectomy TE-based reconstruction were included. Outcomes of interest included seroma formation, surgical site infection (SSI), hematoma, return to the operating room, skin flap necrosis, drain duration, and TE/implant-related complications. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence with the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Three retrospective observational studies comprising 1350 reconstructions were included, with 660 reconstructions in the single-drain group and 690 in the double-drain group. There were no significant differences between single- and double-drain strategies in seroma formation (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.49; p = 0.54; I² = 63%), SSI (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.37; p = 0.93; I² = 39%), hematoma (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.44 to 1.63; p = 0.61; I² = 0%), return to the operating room (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.30 to 1.43; p = 0.29; I² = 12%), skin flap necrosis (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.46 to 1.19; p = 0.22; I² = 0%), or drain duration (MD -3.90 days, 95% CI -12.42 to 4.63; p = 0.37; I² = 97%). Leave-one-out analyses did not materially alter the findings for seroma formation or SSI. Certainty of evidence was low for seroma, SSI, and skin flap necrosis, and very low for hematoma, return to the operating room, and drain duration.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a benefit of routine double-drain placement after TE-based breast reconstruction. The certainty of evidence was low, and these findings indicate a lack of demonstrated benefit rather than equivalence between the two strategies. Selective second-drain placement based on intraoperative findings remains reasonable, and adequately powered prospective studies are needed.

gundem.baslik: Surgical Margin and Risk of Local Recurrence in Children and Young Adults With Nonrhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Nonrhabdomyosarcoma Yumuşak Doku Sarkomunda Cerrahi Sınır
gundem.kisa_ozet: 266 hastada yapılan prospektif çalışmada, nonrhabdomyosarcoma yumuşak doku sarkomu için R0 rezeksiyon sonrası 5 yıllık lokal nüks insidansı %4,4 bulundu. 6 mm ve üzeri cerrahi sınırlarda nüks izlenmezken, 1 mm'de %4,9, 2-5 mm'de %2,0 olarak saptandı. Geniş cerrahi sınırlar lokal nüks riskini daha da azaltmaktadır.
gundem.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: The extent of negative margin necessary to achieve a high rate of local tumor control in children and young adult patients with nonrhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcomas (NRSTS) is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of negative margin extent on local tumor control in children and young adult patients with NRSTS undergoing R0 resection as part of risk-adapted multimodality treatment.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter prospective clinical trial was conducted at Children's Oncology Group (COG) member sites from February 2007 through February 2012. Analysis was performed on the final dataset June 30, 2018, with a median follow-up of 6.2 years. Reviewers of margin status/extent were blinded to local control outcomes. Patients included 266 eligible/evaluable individuals younger than 30 years with nonmetastatic NRSTS who were enrolled in the COG ARST0332 trial and underwent upfront or delayed R0 resection as part of treatment. Patients who underwent an amputation or did not receive protocol-specified radiotherapy were excluded. These data were analyzed from January 2023 through July 2026.
INTERVENTION: Risk-adapted treatment included 3 patient groups with upfront or delayed surgery with or without radiation therapy with or without ifosfamide/doxorubicin chemotherapy, based on the extent of initial resection, surgical margin status, tumor size, and histologic grade.
MAIN OUTCOMES: Cumulative incidence of local recurrence based on treatment approach and surgical margin extent and outcomes after local recurrence.
RESULTS: Of 266 patients (median age 13.7 [range, 2.1-27.6] years; 138 female [52%] and 128 male [48%]) who underwent upfront (n = 207) or delayed (n = 59) R0 resection, 132 had measured surgical margins: 1 mm (n = 56), 2 to 5 mm (n = 50), or 6-mm or larger (n = 26). The 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence overall was 4.4%. Local recurrence occurred in 10 of 178 patients treated with surgery alone (5.6%) and 2 of 88 patients treated with surgery and chemoradiotherapy (2.3%). Among the 132 patients with measured surgical margins, the 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence was 4.9% for 1-mm margins, 2.0% for 2- to 5-mm margins, and 0% for 6-mm or larger margins. Local recurrence occurred in 10 of 178 (5.6%) patients with tumors smaller than 5 cm treated with margin-negative surgery alone, 1 of 29 (3.4%) patients with tumors larger than 5 cm treated with margin-negative surgery followed by chemoradiotherapy, and 1 of 59 (1.7%) patients with initially unresectable disease treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Five of 12 patients with local recurrence were alive without further disease progression.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, the local recurrence rate after R0 resection among children and young adult patients treated with risk-based therapy for nonmetastatic NRSTS was low, and some patients underwent successful salvage therapy with durable long-term disease control. Wider (>1 mm) negative margins further decrease local recurrence risk. Close surgical margins may be adequate in some clinical settings, particularly in the context of chemoradiotherapy, according to a risk-adapted approach.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT00346164.

gundem.baslik: Long-term oncological outcomes of robotic versus laparoscopic total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer: COLRAR randomized clinical trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Rektum kanserinde robotik ve laparoskopik TME'nin uzun dönem sonuçları: COLRAR RCT
gundem.kisa_ozet: 295 rektum kanserli hastanın dahil edildiği çok merkezli RCT'de, 5 yıllık genel sağkalım (%92,6'ya karşı %92,4; p=0,838) ve hastalıksız sağkalım (%81,9'a karşı %83,0; p=0,801) R-TME ve L-TME gruplarında benzer bulunmuştur. Neoadjuvan KRT alan 146 hastada, 5 yıllık lokal nükssüz sağkalım R-TME ile %98,6, L-TME ile %90,7 saptanmıştır (p=0,039).
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Long-term oncological equivalence of robotic total mesorectal excision (R-TME) and laparoscopic total mesorectal excision (L-TME) remains unproven. The 5-year outcomes of the COLRAR RCT are reported.
METHODS: Adults with cT1-4a Nx M0 rectal adenocarcinoma within 10 cm of the anal verge were randomized 1 : 1 to L-TME or R-TME at three Korean tertiary centres between July 2011 and February 2016. Pre-specified secondary endpoints were 5-year overall, relapse-free, local recurrence-free, and distant recurrence-free survival. Analyses were on a modified intention-to-treat basis.
RESULTS: Of 295 analysed patients (144 L-TME patients and 151 R-TME patients; median follow-up of 72.6 months), 5-year overall survival (92.6% versus 92.4%; P = 0.838) and relapse-free survival (81.9% versus 83.0%; P = 0.801) were similar. Local recurrence occurred in 4.9% (L-TME) and 1.3% (R-TME); 5-year local recurrence-free and distant recurrence-free survival did not differ (P = 0.076 and P = 0.655). In a post-hoc analysis of 146 patients who received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, 5-year local recurrence-free survival was 98.6% in R-TME patients versus 90.7% in L-TME patients (P = 0.039).
CONCLUSION: R-TME and L-TME produced equivalent 5-year oncological outcomes. A post-hoc analysis suggested improved local control with robotic surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, requiring confirmation in prospectively designed studies.
REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT01423214 (http://www.clinicaltrials.gov).

gundem.baslik: Efficacy of indocyanine green (ICG) angiography in reducing postoperative complications in oesophagectomy: systematic review and meta-analysis.
gundem.baslik_tr: Özofajektomide ICG Anjiyografinin Anastomotik Kaçak Üzerine Etkisi
gundem.kisa_ozet: 2845 hastayı içeren 23 çalışmanın yer aldığı meta-analizde, özofajektomide ICG kullanımı anastomotik kaçak oranlarında azalma ile ilişkili bulunmuştur (OR 0,44; p<0,001). Ayrıca kondükt nekrozu da ICG grubunda daha düşük saptanmıştır (OR 0,32; p=0,022).
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leakage after oesophagectomy is common, and associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography has emerged as a promising intraoperative adjunct for perfusion assessment at the anastomotic site. This study aims to assess the impact of ICG use on anastomotic leakage rates and postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic search of Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library was performed. The primary outcome was anastomotic leakage. Key secondary outcomes were conduit necrosis, mortality, and reoperation; all secondary outcomes were reported. The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tools were used for investigating risk of bias. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) was used to assess certainty of evidence. A random-effects meta-analysis and meta-regression as well as subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: From 902 identified studies, 23 met the inclusion criteria (including 4 RCTs; 2845 patients, of whom 1154 underwent ICG assessment). ICG use was associated with reduced anastomotic leakage rates (OR 0.44 (95% c.i. 0.29 to 0.65), P < 0.001; number needed to treat = 13) and conduit necrosis rates (OR 0.32 (95% c.i. 0.12 to 0.85), P = 0.022). Mortality (OR 1.43 (95% c.i. 0.69 to 2.97), P = 0.335), reoperation (OR 0.84 (95% c.i. 0.51 to 1.39), P = 0.500), severe anastomotic leakage, overall morbidity, readmission, operating time, and length of stay did not differ between groups. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes (GRADE), predominantly driven by the observational study design of many of the studies.
CONCLUSION: Use of ICG appears to be associated with reduced anastomotic leak in oesophagectomy, although certainty of evidence is low. Assessment remains qualitative and operator-dependent.

gundem.baslik: Small-bite compared with large-bite closure of midline laparotomy: meta-analysis of short- and long-term outcomes with trial sequential analysis.
gundem.baslik_tr: Orta Hat Laparotomilerde Küçük ve Büyük Isırık Fasyal Kapama Karşılaştırılması: Meta-Analiz
gundem.kisa_ozet: 10 RCT ve 2617 hastayı kapsayan meta-analizde, orta hat laparotomilerinde küçük ısırık tekniği insizyonel herni riskini %43 azaltmıştır (RR 0,57; %95 CI 0,39-0,82; p=0,003). Ayrıca SSI (RR 0,72) ve toplam komplikasyonlar (RR 0,76) azalmış, kapama süresi ise 4,82 dakika uzamıştır. Fayda 2 yılı aşan takipte de devam etmiştir.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Fascial closure after a midline laparotomy (ML) is a crucial step to avoid incisional hernia. This meta-analysis aimed to compare short- and long-term outcomes, including incisional hernia, of the small-bite versus large-bite closure techniques in ML.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of RCTs comparing small-bite (5-mm bites/spacing) and large-bite (10-mm bites/spacing) techniques in ML closure was conducted. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central were searched from inception through April 2026 for eligible RCTs. The primary outcome was incisional hernia. Secondary outcomes included total complications, surgical-site infection (SSI), seroma, fascial dehiscence, closure time, and pain. Pairwise meta-analyses and trial sequential analyses (TSA) were performed.
RESULTS: Ten unique RCTs reported in 12 publications (2617 patients) were included. Among the five studies using standardized clinical and imaging assessment, small-bite closure reduced incisional hernia by 43% (risk ratio (RR) of 0.57 (95% c.i. 0.39 to 0.82) (P = 0.003, I2 = 44.1%), compared with an RR of 0.31 (95% c.i. 0.18 to 0.53) (P < 0.001, I2 = 0) when clinical assessment only was used). Across all eligible studies with follow-up >12 months, the pooled RR was 0.48 (95% c.i. 0.33 to 0.70). This benefit persisted on the analysis of studies with ≥24 months of follow-up (RR 0.56 (95% c.i. 0.36 to 0.89)). TSA demonstrated firm evidence for benefit despite not reaching the required information size. Small-bite closure was also associated with reduced SSI (RR 0.72) and total complications (RR 0.76), with no differences in seroma or fascial dehiscence. Closure time was slightly longer with small-bite closure (weighted mean difference 4.82 min), while pain scores were comparable.
CONCLUSION: The small-bite technique significantly reduced incisional hernia and postoperative complications after ML, with durable benefit extending beyond 2 years.

gundem.baslik: WSES-PSOGI-SICO evidence-infomed guidelines on surgical emergencies in patients with peritoneal surface malignancies: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and structured expert consensus.
gundem.baslik_tr: Peritoneal Malignitelerde Acil Cerrahi Yönetimi İçin WSES-PSOGI-SICO Kılavuzu
gundem.kisa_ozet: Sistemik derleme, meta-analiz ve uzman konsensüsü ile peritoneal malignitelerle ilişkili malign barsak obstrüksiyonunun acil yönetimi incelenmiştir. Tıbbi tedavi daha düşük morbidite sağlarken, cerrahi daha yüksek klinik başarı (OR 2,57; %95 CI 1,47-4,50) göstermiştir. Tüm kılavuz önermeleri %100 uzlaşıya ulaşmıştır.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM) are primary or secondary neoplastic deposits involving the peritoneum and are commonly associated with colorectal, gastric, appendiceal, gynecological, pancreaticobiliary, and other intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal cancers. Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is one of the most frequent and clinically consequential emergency presentations in this population, yet diagnostic and therapeutic pathways remain heterogeneous. We aimed to develop evidence-informed recommendations for emergency management of MBO in patients with PSM by integrating a systematic review, meta-analysis and a structured international expert consensus process.
METHODS: This systematic review, meta-analysis, and Delphi consensus followed PRISMA, Cochrane, and relevant MOOSE reporting principles. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2025 (English language). Five predefined PICO/PIRT questions addressed: (1) the diagnostic role of CT, plain abdominal X-ray, or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; (2) nonoperative medical management versus surgical or endoscopic therapy; (3) surgical versus endoscopic treatment after failure of nonoperative management; (4) bowel resection versus stoma or bypass in surgical candidates; and (5) endoscopic stenting versus endoscopic ultrasound-guided bypass with lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic candidates. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and MINORS for non-comparative studies; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML) produced odds ratios (OR), mean differences (MD), pooled means, or pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was summarized using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Evidence profiles informed statements voted on by the WSES-PSOGI-SICO expert panel during the 2025 WSES Congress.
RESULTS: No comparative diagnostic study evaluated abdominal X-ray or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; two small retrospective CT-based series supported contrast-enhanced CT for mapping obstruction and excluding urgent complications, but no diagnostic meta-analysis was possible. For medical versus procedural treatment, medical management was associated with lower morbidity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07-0.39) and shorter length of stay (MD - 9.48 days, 95% CI - 12.65 to -6.32), while success, mortality, and overall survival remained inconclusive. For surgery versus endoscopy, surgery showed higher clinical success (OR 2.57, 95% CI 1.47-4.50), whereas endoscopy shortened hospital stay (MD 3.35 days, 95% CI 1.46-5.23); mortality did not differ (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70-1.49). Among surgical options, resection showed a signal toward higher perioperative mortality than bypass or ostomy (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.45-8.68). Endoscopic stenting showed a pooled clinical success rate of 0.71 (95% CI 0.62-0.79), whereas evidence on LAMS was limited to one retrospective study. All guideline statements reached 100% agreement among voting participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the low certainty of available evidence, integration of systematic review findings with expert consensus provides a structured international framework to support decision-making in emergency presentations of PSM-related MBO. These consensus-based recommendations are intended to assist clinicians in harmonizing care across peripheral and referral hospitals, while emphasizing individualized multidisciplinary judgement and the need for future higher-quality evidence.
gundem.dergi_tam: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
